item.title: Lions’ Jared Goff downplays Bears’ role in false start woes, but Detroit O-Lineman isn’t as kind

As the Detroit Lions collapsed to the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day on Thursday, losing 39-35, there is a conversation around the self-inflicted mistakes that the team went through that led to the defeat. While the Lions and Bears game will be remembered for Chicago scoring 29 points in the second half, there is also the topic of Detroit’s false start penalties, which led to an interesting comment from quarterback Jared Goff . The Lions committed four false start penalties, with Juice Scruggs charged with three of them and Christian Mahogany getting the other, as the latter said that players on Chicago were “emulating snap counts.” “No b****ing and complaining. We had self-inflicted wounds,’ Mahogany said. ‘The league can investigate.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mahogany said that “the guards wear microphones, so that you can hear the QB on TV,” further saying that “they’ll be able to hear “clear as day” what was going on, according to Brad Galli. Goff would downplay the situation: “I don’t think that should be overblown. I think it happened a couple times,” Goff said, via Galli. “The officials talked to them, and if they were trying to simulate the snap count, or if they weren’t, I don’t know, they can probably say they aren’t; it’s impossible to officiate, and they’ll never throw a flag on it. It happens. This isn’t the first game it’s happened. We got to be able to handle that a little bit better than we did.” Bears’ Jeffery Simmons responds to Lions’ Christian Mahogany The Lions’ qualms received a response from the Bears, specifically star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who said that “there’s a lot of crying on that side of the ball when that happened,” according to MLive.com. “But as a defensive lineman, when your quarterback checks, I’m allowed to say he can check into a run. When Jared checked, and I said, ‘It’s a run; they’re checking to a run,’ it’s not my fault your center jumped,” Simmons said. At any rate, Detroit let go of the rope after a 19-10 halftime lead and now is 8-3 on the season, putting them second in the NFC North. item.title: Dylan Harper could be back in action when Spurs host Lakers on Friday
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper reacts to a 3-pointer by teammate Julian Champagnie, not pictured, during the fourth quarter of an NBA game against the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, in San Antonio. The Spurs won 124-112. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs guard Dylan Harper could make his return to the court as soon as Friday night after the team listed him as questionable for its showdown with the Los Angeles Lakers at the Frost Bank Center. Harper has missed the last four games after he suffered a left hip external rotator strain late in the Spurs' 105-93 loss to Detroit on Nov. 17. The injury was expected to sideline him for two to three weeks, but the Spurs upgraded him to questionable after Wednesday night's 116-111 loss at Portland. Harper, 20, ranks as the Spurs' second-leading scorer behind Victor Wembanyama at 18.4 points per game. He's also averaging 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 15 appearances. The Spurs are 3-1 without Harper, who has been replaced in the starting lineup by Julian Champagnie. In other injury news, the Spurs upgraded guard De'Aaron Fox to questionable after he sat out the last two games with a bruised right shin. The Spurs started Harrison Barnes the last two games to round out a starting lineup that included Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell, Champagnie and Wembanyama. Forward Tobias Harris remains out with a left calf strain. The 15-year-veteran suffered the injury early in training camp after the Spurs signed him in the offseason to a two-year, $31 million contract. Ezra Frech was recently crowned the Dancing with the Stars Season 35 winner alongside Daniella Karagach, and Travis Kelce made a recent social media move in support of his historic feat. item.title: Why even Trent Williams envies the high point of new 49ers starter Vederian Lowe's career
item.description: San Francisco 49ers offensive tackle Vederian Lowe (76) blocks during an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. (AP Photo/Scot Tucker) (Scot Tucker/AP) Vederian Lowe has picked Trent Williams ' brain and studied the generational left tackle's film since signing with the San Francisco 49ers in March, but the onetime sixth-round pick and part-time NFL starter understands there are limits to what he can replicate. "A lot of the things that he does, I can't do," Lowe said. "Because Trent is one of one." However, there is something Lowe has done that Williams has spent his illustrious 16-season career wishing he could do. On Nov. 17, 2024, Lowe, then with the Patriots, realized every 300-pound man's dream when he caught a 4-yard touchdown from quarterback Drake Maye in a loss to the Chargers. Asked where his lone catch ranks among his career highlights, Lowe smiled and invoked Williams, who is catch-less and has long lobbied head coach Kyle Shanahan for a goal-line pass. "That (catch) might be number one because they don't come by - I was talking to Trent and even Trent doesn't have one," Lowe said. "So I'm like, ‘OK.' That's up there for sure." The lofty ranking Lowe has assigned his reception speaks to the rarity of such a snag. But it also speaks to the modest number of highlights he's collected in a five-season career that has included 25 starts, just four since Jan. 5, 2025. But that could be changing. Last Sunday, in a 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City, Lowe was unexpectedly thrust into the role of a key starter on a Super Bowl contender when right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a broken and dislocated ankle in the second quarter . McKivitz's season is over. Lowe's chance to show why the 49ers signed him to a two-year contract with a maximum value of $12 million to serve as their swing tackle is just beginning. "That's why we brought him here," Shanahan said. "Anytime you have a swing tackle - that means you better be capable of starting. He's started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter. And that's why we targeted him." Lowe is assuming some sizable cleats. McKivitz, 30, was earning every bit of the three-year, $45 million extension he signed last year by not allowing a sack in 327 pass-blocking snaps this season before his injury. The very early returns, however, are promising. On Lowe's first snap after replacing McKivitz, he pancaked defensive tackle Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins on a 10-yard run by Christian McCaffrey . It was the start of a 38-snap performance in which Lowe committed a false start, but he didn't allow a QB pressure on 19 pass-blocking snaps against Minnesota's chaotic, blitz-heavy defense, a unit which leads the NFL in sacks. Lowe did so despite logging most of his snaps at left tackle throughout his career. item.description: LANDOVER, MD – DECEMBER 25: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams 33 reads his blockers during game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Washington Commanders on December 25, 2025 at Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD. Photo by Charles Brock/Icon Sportswire NFL, American Football Herren, USA DEC 25 Cowboys at Commanders EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon251225004 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire An officiating decision in the Eagles-Cowboys game has put the NFL’s review process under scrutiny again. Philadelphia’s touchdown, which came after a Javonte Williams fumble, was taken off the board by the officials, and the play never counted. The officials’ interpretation of forward progress is disputed; some analysts argue Williams did fumble before being ruled down. Nevertheless, the ruling has now prompted fans and analysts to question how the rule was applied and whether the league enforces it consistently across games. “Whistle halts Riq Woolen return after Javonte Williams fumble. Nick Sirianni protested the early stoppage,” Wire Report NFL posted on X . Williams was driving toward the end zone when the ball came loose just short of the goal line in the second quarter. Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen scooped it up and took off for a 97-yard return that looked like a touchdown. Before he got there, the whistle blew. The officials ruled that Williams’ forward progress had already been stopped, which meant the play was dead before Woolen reached the end zone, preventing a TD rather than erasing one. When a touchdown gets erased in a rivalry game, the entire playoff picture shifts. Stay ahead of every controversial call and its impact with EssentiallySports NFL coverage. That ruling carries a harsh consequence, because forward progress calls can’t be challenged. Nick Sirianni had nothing to throw a flag over and no review to ask for, so the Eagles simply had to line up again. Dallas then scored its own touchdown to build the halftime cushion. By the start of the fourth quarter, the Cowboys led 31-17, with Philadelphia having added ten points in the second quarter and seven in the third. The officials’ call on it is now drawing heavy criticism. One fan, whose comment was originally in Spanish, summed up how it looked from the stands: “To me, this was a fumble by Javonte Williams and a potential defensive TD for the Eagles that would have made it 21-17 at halftime. The refs blew the whistle (too early, in my opinion), and that killed the play. Anyway… on to the next one.” Media voices were just as direct. item.title: Tom Brady breaks his silence with scathing Aaron Rodgers verdict live on Fox
item.description: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images Just about everyone has had their say on Aaron Rodgers’ blockbuster interview on The Pat McAfee Show. Now, Tom Brady has broken his silence on the saga. Rodgers cleared waivers on Thursday afternoon, with the Pittsburgh Steelers preparing for their game on Friday against the Denver Broncos. Whether a team will even look to bring him into their building on the back of his explosive interview remains a huge unknown. The interview on McAfee’s show has certainly split opinions, with some people welcoming the honesty from the future Hall of Famer. Brady does not seem to fall on that side of the divide, with the former quarterback sharing his thoughts on Fox Sports’ coverage of the Dallas Cowboys vs Philadelphia Eagles. What Tom Brady said about Aaron Rodgers’ Mike McCarthy comments No one needs reminding of what Rodgers said on The Pat McAfee Show, with his comments being the major talking point across the NFL over the last 24 hours. Brady was left far from impressed, with the 49-year-old finally speaking out on the matter. “Yeah, and that’s one thing I just think in response to that: the sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, and you’re always acting as a team together. It shouldn’t be a place for private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say,” Brady said on Fox Sports. This has been a running theme with a lot of former players and coaches, with Rob Gronkowski also unimpressed with Rodgers . For some, the 42-year-old has only spoken the harsh truths, but for others, he has broken the trust of an NFL locker room. “Certainly a Hall of Fame career, and he’s a tremendous player. And that’s not going to detract from what he plays for, which is a fortunate lot of teammates over the years. What made him a great teammate was that he cared about his teammates,” Brady added. Given the view of Brady and some other former players and coaches, it is difficult to see how Rodgers would be accepted by another team before the end of the season. It really does look like this is how he is going to bow out of his incredible NFL career. The Patriots are slated to play the lowly Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday as they try to course-correct their season after losing starting quarterback Drake Maye, and the team’s defense is expected to be a large part of that equation. item.title: Australia's sandpapergate probe to also include 2017-18 Ashes
item.description: Australia won the 2017-18 Ashes series against England 4-0 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England. The terms of reference for the independent forum have been published and the scope will include "ball-management practices in the Australian men's team during the 2017–18 season", which includes the Ashes series Australia won 4-0. Also included are all four Tests of the subsequent South Africa tour and the investigation which followed when the ball-tampering scandal emerged. Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report and recommendations within 30 days of receiving them. All those involved in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa will be invited to speak to the independent forum, though none will have to do so and no retrospective sanctions will be handed out. The scandal was reignited by the release of former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography. In it, Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about ball-tampering in the third Test of their series against South Africa in Cape Town. The four frontline bowlers in that 2018 team - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and current Test captain Pat Cummins - have always denied knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball. Cummins has called Khawaja's recollection of events "nonsense". However, former team-mates David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of three players who were banned for their part in the scandal, alongside Steve Smith - have backed Khawaja's version of events. "All participants in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa, including players and support staff, will be invited to take part in the Independent Forum, as will CA management and directors at that time," Cricket Australia said. "While all involved will be encouraged to participate, there will be no compulsion to do so. All materials supplied will be treated as confidential unless otherwise stated by the participant and no sanctions will be retrospectively applied. "Participants can choose to attend the Independent Forum in person, online and/or provide information via written accounts or through relevant documents and materials." The forum will be open for six weeks. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA Board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," CA chair David Boon said. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn. "Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. "It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate." Cummins retains Cricket

Indeed, BVB are enjoying a historically strong first half of the season. For only the third time in their Bundesliga history, the Black & Yellows are unbeaten after ten matches. They previously achieved this only in 2002/03 under Matthias Sammer and in 2018/19 under Lucien Favre. Another win would take Borussia Dortmund to 27 points – their highest tally after 11 matches in eight years. That makes the difference between the goalkeepers all the more striking. Gregor Kobel has saved 81 per cent of the shots on his goal, compared with just 58 per cent for Leverkusen’s Mark Flekken – the lowest save rate of any Bundesliga goalkeeper. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
